title: Close repo-local callback dispatcher lifecycle
objective: Close the actual callback-delivery gap. AIWorkHub currently persists terminal events but leaves them pending because no callback dispatcher is owned by the VS Code extension lifecycle. Start exactly one repository-bound dispatcher after an initialized workspace becomes active, preserve pending delivery while a coordinator turn/transport is busy, route by the explicitly selected Codex or Claude coordinator target using only existing canonical transports, and stop/rebind cleanly on deactivate, reload or repository switch. Do not add a systemd dependency or a fallback database. Preserve compact callback envelopes and make health distinguish durable queued work from a broken dispatcher.
acceptance: An initialized repository starts exactly one callback dispatcher through the VS Code extension lifecycle; no user systemd unit, manual daemon command or dashboard HTTP server is required.
Activation, editor-tab deserialization and reload converge idempotently on one live repository-bound dispatcher, without duplicate polling loops or duplicate delivery.
Workspace/repository switch and extension deactivation stop the old dispatcher and prevent any cross-repository read or delivery.

The explicitly selected coordinator target controls routing: Codex uses the existing canonical Codex transport; Claude uses the versioned aiworkhub.claude_callback.v1 transport accepted in B856. Unsupported Copilot routing fails closed and remains visible without fabricating delivery.
Busy, temporarily unavailable or active-turn transports keep terminal callbacks pending with bounded backoff; they do not dead-letter or return tasks to pending.
A matching transport acknowledgement is required before the canonical outbox row is marked delivered; restarts safely recover leases and never duplicate an acknowledged callback.
Callback payloads remain compact: batch count and task_id/state lines only, with no worker output, logs, artifacts, prompts or objective text.

Dashboard/runtime health reports dispatcher running/stopped, target, repository identity, pending count and last delivery/error without marking an otherwise healthy uninitialized repository as degraded.
The public task lifecycle and callback status remain on the selected repository's .aiworkhub/tasking/task_queue.sqlite and do not invoke repository AITools/taskctl.py or AITools/taskdb.py.
The stale subprocess expectation in test_server_runtime_wiring.py is rebased to the canonical in-process engine contract.
Focused Python, Node and VSIX packaging tests pass. Codex can then run one real terminal-task canary and observe pending-to-delivered plus a callback in the bound coordinator thread.
